text: Spellguard
He is slow and lightly armoured, so his wards do the work. Spells and arrows land softer on him.
Focused Bolt
He stops throwing the Winds and starts aiming them.
Long Reach
He casts from further back and carries more charges for the staff.
Wind Blast
When the enemy reaches him anyway, the staff blasts them back.
Hedge Wards
Small charms tied to every banner pole, against hostile magic.
Screen the Staff
His soldiers learn to stand between him and the enemy, and he keeps them covered in return.
Woven Wards
He threads a ward through every rank before the first blow.
Channelled Staff
The staff draws in the Winds and fires them back as five bolts at once.
Charged Steel
Before the lines meet he walks along them and touches every blade.
Shield Wall
He stands where the blows land thickest and lets them come.
Turn the Arrow
He keeps the shield high, and arrows find wood instead of him.
Iron Body
He was never quick. He learned to be hard to kill instead.
Bulwark
He plants his feet, and nothing on the field can shift him.
Hold the Line
Men stand firm next to a man who will not step back.
Shields Up
He calls the volley before the archers loose.
Locked Shields
Every shield overlaps the next, the way he showed them.
Shield of Faith
His faith is not in any god. It is in the hope that this time will end differently.
Guardian
Whoever stands behind him is out of reach. He makes sure of it.
Steady Draw
He breathes out, and the arrow goes where he looked.
Hunter's Blade
When something big gets close, the short blade is ready.
Long Eye
He shoots from further out and faster, and carries extra arrows for a long hunt.
Executioner's Shot
One arrow, saved for the biggest thing on the field.
Huntsmen
He shows the archers where to aim.
Marked Ground
Every stone and stake is a range marker to him, and every cart carries spare shafts.
Trueshot
Archers near him shoot as if he were checking every shot.
Hunter's Spread
He nocks six arrows at once and looses them all.
Loose!
Nock, draw, loose. He counts it out until they no longer need him to.
Overhand
A blow from above, with all of him behind it.
Wide Arc
He swings to hit several men at once, not just one.
Cleaving Arc
One swing, three men. He has done the sums.
Headsman
A killing blow for anyone who stands in front of him too long.
Bloody Drill
He makes them practise until they stop flinching.
Charge Them
He goes first. They follow, and they keep swinging.
Through the Plate
He teaches them where the armour is thinnest.
Whirl of Steel
He stops choosing targets and lets the blade go round.
Butcher's Bill
He knows what this battle will cost, and makes the enemy pay it first.
Horse Cutter
The glaive was made for one job: rider and horse, in one stroke.
Through the Barding
He finds the gap in a war beast's armour on the first try.
Turning Blade
The heavy head keeps moving after the cut, and whatever stands in its arc goes down with it.
Beastslayer
To him, monsters are just very large men. The glaive has the reach for them.
Long Arms
He teaches every unit where to stand when the big ones come.
Light Kit
Half the baggage, twice the marching. They arrive fresh.
Find the Gap
Every plate has a seam, and he shows his men where to find it.
Wall of Blades
He has seen this kind of charge before. He sets his line so it breaks on them.
Ten Thousand Blades
He fights like the glaive lines that once stopped an empire's cavalry, all on his own.
Iron Skin
Blows ring off him like a hammer off an anvil.
Forge Palm
An open hand that lands with the weight of a falling ingot.
Hammer Hands
Each strike falls like the smith's hammer, and the men around the one he hits feel it too.
Unbending
He takes the hit and does not move a step, however hard it lands.
Foundry Drill
He works his soldiers like iron, heat and hammer, and they learn faster from every fight.
Tempered Ranks
Broken units are mended and sent back to the line, harder than before.
Old Hands
New recruits are put next to his veterans from the first day, and they learn fast.
Cast in Iron
He drills every unit like the company he once led. They take a blow the way iron takes the hammer.
Battering Ram
He lowers his shoulder and walks into the enemy line, and the line gives way.
